newsitem.title: USA: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, Mar hits new low.
newsitem.headline: Most NYMEX Hub natgas ends down, Mar hits new low.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended steady to lower Monday in an active session, with spot-March driven to a new contract low late in the day by a flood of technical selling and long liquidation, sources said.

March expired 15.6 cents lower at $1.78 per million British thermal units after sinking late to a new contract low of $1.68. April settled 10.4 cents lower at $1.815. Other months ended steady to down by 7.5 cents.

"The sellers didn't blink and the longs get creamed at the end. Fundamentals are telling you this could be the high price for the month - there's no weather and there aren't going to be any storage surprises," said one Midwest trader.
With storage in good shape, most agreed a brief cold snap early this week in the Midwest and Northeast was not enough to rally prices, particularly with a warm up expected later in the week.

And while technical traders were still expecting a short covering bounce, most saw more downside ahead after March and April blew through key support points today. Next support for April was seen in the mid-$1.70s and then at the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was pegged at $2.04 and $2.16.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were talked on either side of $1.90 Monday, little changed on the day. Midcon pipes firmed slightly to the mid-$1.70s. Cold weather boosted New York city gate gas prices by 10 cents to the mid-$2.20s.
The 12-month strip fell 3.8 cents to $2.018. NYMEX said an estimated 74,122 Hub contracts traded, up sharply from Friday's revised tally of 47,868.
NYMEX Permian and Alberta natgas did not trade Monday.

On the KCBT, March, which expires Tuesday, finished 10 cents lower at $1.55, while deferreds ended down by 2.5 to 10 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 5.6 cents to 23 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 523 lots changed hands, up .cfrom Friday's total of 220.
